name: Pricing & Packaging Research
description: Design pricing and packaging from customer value, segmentation, willingness-to-pay evidence, unit economics, competitive context, and controlled validation rather than copying a competitor’s table.

tasks.name: Map customer value
tasks.objective: Define segments, jobs, alternatives, value drivers, usage patterns, economic outcomes, adoption barriers, and plausible value metrics. Separate value created from cost-to-serve.

tasks.name: Collect pricing evidence
tasks.objective: Use interviews, win-loss, sales objections, usage/cohort data, historical price changes, competitor packaging, deal data, and appropriate willingness-to-pay research. Record sample and method limits.

tasks.name: Choose price metric and fences
tasks.objective: Evaluate seats, usage, outcomes, capacity, tiers, add-ons, minimums, and entitlement fences for alignment with customer value, predictability, expansion, cost, abuse, and implementation complexity.

tasks.name: Design package architecture
tasks.objective: Create coherent good/better/best or modular packages around segment needs, not arbitrary feature withholding; define upgrade logic, grandfathering/migration, trials, discounts, and enterprise exceptions.

tasks.name: Model economics and scenarios
tasks.objective: Model revenue, gross margin, usage distribution, support burden, discounting, cannibalization, expansion, churn sensitivity, and extreme-use cases across price/package options.

tasks.name: Validate in market
tasks.objective: Use controlled experiments, new-cohort rollouts, quote tests, sales simulations, or phased changes appropriate to risk. Monitor conversion, activation, expansion, churn, support load, and qualitative confusion.

tasks.name: Publish pricing decision system
tasks.objective: Document package definitions, price metric, evidence, economics, migration rules, discount governance, measurement plan, and review triggers. Preserve uncertainty and regional/segment differences.
